title: Accumulator
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Buys one share a week at a discount to the initial level, twice as many when the stock is below that price, until it closes at or above the knock-out level.

params.name: strike
params.label: Purchase price, % of the initial level

params.name: knock_out
params.label: Knock-out level, % of the initial level

params.name: gearing
params.label: Shares bought below the strike, per share above

script:
# Weekly for six months. Each purchase is marked at the close: its value is
# (spot - strike) per share, paid on the purchase date. The knock-out is
# checked first: no purchase on the day it knocks out.

2027-01-04
    strike = 0.9
    knock_out = 1.05
    gearing = 2
    s0 = spot()
    k = strike * s0
    alive = 1

schedule(2027-01-11, 2027-06-28, 1W, US, F)
    if spot() >= knock_out * s0 then alive = 0 endIf
    if alive = 1 then
        if spot() >= k then pays spot() - k else pays gearing * (spot() - k) endIf
    endIf

2027-07-06
    if spot() >= knock_out * s0 then alive = 0 endIf
    if alive = 1 then
        if spot() >= k then pays spot() - k else pays gearing * (spot() - k) endIf
    endIf

title: Altiplano
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A capital-protected note paying a large coupon if none of three stocks ever closes a month below the barrier; otherwise a basket call instead.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Barrier on each stock, % of its initial level

script:
# Monthly monitoring of each stock against its own strike-date level.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.2
    barrier = 0.8
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)
    breached = 0

schedule(2027-02-04, 2027-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    if spot(0) < barrier * s0 or spot(1) < barrier * s1 or spot(2) < barrier * s2 then breached = 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot(0) < barrier * s0 or spot(1) < barrier * s1 or spot(2) < barrier * s2 then breached = 1 endIf
    basket = (spot(0) / s0 + spot(1) / s1 + spot(2) / s2) / 3
    if breached = 0 then
        pays notional * (1 + coupon)
    else
        pays notional * (1 + max(basket - 1, 0))
    endIf

title: American call
sources: Longstaff & Schwartz, Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach, Review of Financial Studies 14(1), 2001
Merton, Theory of Rational Option Pricing, Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science 4(1), 1973
summary: The right to buy the stock at the strike on any week until expiry: worth more than the European call only on a dividend payer, whose holder may exercise to collect the dividends.
script:
# Exercise every week, decided by a least-squares regression of the
# continuation value on the moneyness spot / s0. Exercising is ever worth it
# only in the money and above the forward held to the expiry: the option is
# worth at least (fwd(T) - K) df(T), what holding the stock to expiry and
# paying the strike then is worth now, dividends forgone. Only there is it
# considered, so that the estimated rule never exercises where holding is
# certainly better -- without that bound, on a small dividend, it priced
# under the European. Without dividends it never exercises (Merton 1973).
# The price is a lower bound: the rule is estimated.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()
    done = 0

schedule(2027-01-11, 2027-12-27, 1W, US, F)
    if spot() > strike * s0 and spot() - strike * s0 > (fwd(2028-01-04) - strike * s0) * df(2028-01-04) and exercise(spot() / s0) then
        pays spot() - strike * s0
        done = 1
    endIf

2028-01-04
    if done = 0 then
        pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)
    endIf

title: American put
sources: Longstaff & Schwartz, Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach, Review of Financial Studies 14(1), 2001
Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 21 and 27
summary: The right to sell the stock at the strike on any week until expiry: worth more than the European put, since exercising early collects the strike sooner.
script:
# Exercise every week (a Bermudan standing for continuous exercise), decided
# by a least-squares regression of the continuation value on the moneyness
# spot / s0 (the strike moves with s0, the spot alone would not say how deep
# in the money a path is). Only in the money is exercising ever worth it, so
# only there is it considered: fitting the out-of-the-money paths too bends
# the rule where it matters and prices too low. The price is a lower bound:
# the rule is estimated.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()
    done = 0

schedule(2027-01-11, 2027-12-27, 1W, US, F)
    if spot() < strike * s0 and exercise(spot() / s0) then
        pays strike * s0 - spot()
        done = 1
    endIf

2028-01-04
    if done = 0 then
        pays max(strike * s0 - spot(), 0)
    endIf

title: Arithmetic Asian call
sources: Kemna & Vorst, A Pricing Method for Options Based on Average Asset Values, Journal of Banking & Finance, 1990
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on the average of twelve monthly closes instead of the final price: cheaper than a vanilla, and hard to manipulate at expiry.
script:
# Twelve monthly fixings, the last one on the maturity date.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()
    acc = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-02-04, 2027-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    acc = acc + spot()
    n = n + 1

2028-01-04
    acc = acc + spot()
    n = n + 1
    pays max(acc / n - strike * s0, 0)

title: Averaging-in call
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call whose strike is the average of the first three monthly closes, so a bad entry day does not set the strike.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike, % of the average of the first three fixings

script:
2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    acc = spot()

2027-02-04  2027-03-04
    acc = acc + spot()

2028-01-04
    pays max(spot() - strike * acc / 3, 0)

title: Athena (express) autocall
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Redeemed at the first anniversary the stock is at or above the autocall level, with a coupon per year elapsed; capital at risk below the protection barrier after three years.

params.name: autocall
params.label: Autocall level, % of the initial level

params.name: protection
params.label: Protection barrier at maturity, % of the initial level

script:
# Snowball coupon: the coupon times the number of years at redemption.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.08
    autocall = 1.0
    protection = 0.6
    s0 = spot()
    alive = 1

2028-01-04
    if spot() >= autocall * s0 then
        pays notional * (1 + coupon)
        alive = 0
    endIf

2029-01-04
    if alive = 1 and spot() >= autocall * s0 then
        pays notional * (1 + 2 * coupon)
        alive = 0
    endIf

2030-01-04
    if alive = 1 then
        if spot() >= autocall * s0 then
            pays notional * (1 + 3 * coupon)
        else
            if spot() < protection * s0 then pays notional * spot() / s0 else pays notional endIf
        endIf
    endIf

title: Atlas
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on a four-stock basket from which the best and the worst performers are removed at maturity.
script:
# The basket is the average of the two middle performers.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)
    s3 = spot(3)

2028-01-04
    p0 = spot(0) / s0
    p1 = spot(1) / s1
    p2 = spot(2) / s2
    p3 = spot(3) / s3
    best = max(max(p0, p1), max(p2, p3))
    worst = min(min(p0, p1), min(p2, p3))
    middle = (p0 + p1 + p2 + p3 - best - worst) / 2
    pays notional * max(middle - strike, 0)

title: Barrier reverse convertible
sources: Rubinstein & Reiner, Breaking Down the Barriers, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Quarterly coupons; the capital is at risk only if the stock ever closes at or below the barrier and ends below its initial level.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Knock-in barrier, % of the initial level

script:
# Coupons are paid whatever happens; daily closes for the barrier.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.025
    barrier = 0.6
    s0 = spot()
    ki = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then ki = 1 endIf

2027-04-05  2027-07-06  2027-10-04
    pays notional * coupon

2028-01-04
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then ki = 1 endIf
    pays notional * coupon
    if ki = 1 and spot() < s0 then pays notional * spot() / s0 else pays notional endIf

title: Basket call
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on the equally weighted average performance of three stocks: diversification makes it cheaper than three calls.
script:
# Performance of each stock = final / strike-date level.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)

2028-01-04
    basket = (spot(0) / s0 + spot(1) / s1 + spot(2) / s2) / 3
    pays notional * max(basket - strike, 0)

title: Bermudan swaption
sources: Longstaff & Schwartz, Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach, Review of Financial Studies 14(1), 2001
Brigo & Mercurio, Interest Rate Models - Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., Springer, 2006, ch. 3.3 (Hull-White)
summary: The right to enter, on any of the next five yearly dates from one year out, the SOFR swap at the strike that ends in six years: worth more than each European it contains.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike (fixed rate of the swap entered)

params.name: side
params.label: 1 payer (the right to pay the strike), -1 receiver

script:
# A co-terminal Bermudan: exercising on a fixed date enters the swap's
# remaining periods, worth 1 - P(t, Tn) - strike * annuity(t) per unit of
# notional. The decision is a least-squares regression of the continuation
# value on that exercise value (Hull-White has one factor: the swap's value
# says where the curve is), considered only where exercising pays. The price
# is a lower bound, the rule estimated; the Hull-White lattice prices the
# same trade by backward induction (the test).

2027-01-04
    strike = 0.046
    notional = 10000000
    side = 1

2028-01-04
    value = side * (1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * (yf(2028-01-04, 2029-01-04) * df(2029-01-04) + yf(2029-01-04, 2030-01-04) * df(2030-01-04) + yf(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) * df(2031-01-06) + yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05) + yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)))
    if value > 0 and exercise(value) then
        pays notional * value
    endIf

2029-01-04
    value = side * (1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * (yf(2029-01-04, 2030-01-04) * df(2030-01-04) + yf(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) * df(2031-01-06) + yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05) + yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)))
    if value > 0 and exercise(value) then
        pays notional * value
    endIf

2030-01-04
    value = side * (1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * (yf(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) * df(2031-01-06) + yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05) + yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)))
    if value > 0 and exercise(value) then
        pays notional * value
    endIf

2031-01-06
    value = side * (1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * (yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05) + yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)))
    if value > 0 and exercise(value) then
        pays notional * value
    endIf

2032-01-05
    value = side * (1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * (yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)))
    if value > 0 and exercise(value) then
        pays notional * value
    endIf

title: Best-of call
sources: Stulz, Options on the Minimum or the Maximum of Two Risky Assets, Journal of Financial Economics, 1982
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on the best performer of three stocks: expensive, and worth more the less the stocks move together.
script:
2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)

2028-01-04
    best = max(spot(0) / s0, max(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    pays notional * max(best - strike, 0)

title: Bonus certificate
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Tracks the stock, but pays at least the bonus level if it never closes at or below the barrier.

params.name: bonus
params.label: Bonus level, % of the initial level

script:
# Once the barrier is touched the certificate is plain stock.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    bonus = 1.2
    barrier = 0.7
    s0 = spot()
    hit = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then hit = 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then hit = 1 endIf
    if hit = 0 then
        pays notional * max(spot() / s0, bonus)
    else
        pays notional * spot() / s0
    endIf

title: Call spread (capped call)
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call whose gain is capped: long a call at the strike, short a call at the cap.
script:
2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    cap = 1.2
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays min(max(spot() - strike * s0, 0), (cap - strike) * s0)

title: Capital-protected note
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: The capital back for sure, plus a share of the stock's rise up to a cap: a zero-coupon bond and a call spread.
script:
# Two years, 100% capital protection.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    participation = 0.8
    cap = 0.4
    s0 = spot()

2029-01-04
    pays notional * (1 + participation * min(max(spot() / s0 - 1, 0), cap))

title: Chooser option
sources: Rubinstein, Options for the Undecided, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: On the choice date the holder decides whether the option is a call or a put, both struck at the same level: long volatility without a view on direction.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike of the call and of the put, % of the initial level

script:
# The choice is an early-exercise decision (a Longstaff-Schwartz regression
# on the spot): the price is a lower bound for the holder, priced on the CPU.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()
    is_call = 0

2027-07-06
    if exercise(spot()) then
        is_call = 1
    endIf

2028-01-04
    if is_call = 1 then
        pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)
    else
        pays max(strike * s0 - spot(), 0)
    endIf

title: Locally capped cliquet
sources: Wilmott, Cliquet Options and Volatility Models, Wilmott Magazine, 2002
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Adds up four quarterly returns, each floored and capped: a guaranteed-positive, capped exposure to steady growth.
script:
# Each quarter's return is measured from the previous quarter's close.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    local_floor = 0.0
    local_cap = 0.03
    ref = spot()
    total = 0

2027-04-05  2027-07-06  2027-10-04
    total = total + min(max(spot() / ref - 1, local_floor), local_cap)
    ref = spot()

2028-01-04
    total = total + min(max(spot() / ref - 1, local_floor), local_cap)
    pays notional * total

title: Compound option (call on a call)
sources: Geske, The Valuation of Compound Options, Journal of Financial Economics, 1979
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: The right, on the decision date, to buy a call by paying a premium: leverage on the call itself.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike of the underlying call, % of the initial level

params.name: premium
params.label: Premium paid on the decision date for the call, % of the initial level

script:
# The decision is an early-exercise right (a Longstaff-Schwartz regression on
# the spot): the price is a lower bound for the holder, priced on the CPU.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    premium = 0.05
    s0 = spot()
    held = 0

2027-07-06
    if exercise(spot()) then
        pays -premium * s0
        held = 1
    endIf

2028-01-04
    if held = 1 then pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0) endIf

title: Corridor variance swap
sources: Demeterfi, Derman, Kamal & Zou, A Guide to Volatility and Variance Swaps, Journal of Derivatives, 1999
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A variance swap that only counts the days the stock starts inside a corridor: cheaper downside or upside variance.

params.name: low
params.label: Corridor low, % of the initial level

params.name: high
params.label: Corridor high, % of the initial level

script:
# A return enters the sum only if the previous close was inside the
# corridor; the annualisation still divides by every day observed.

2027-01-04
    variance_notional = 10000
    vol_strike = 0.2
    low = 0.8
    high = 1.2
    s0 = spot()
    prev = spot()
    sumsq = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if prev >= low * s0 and prev <= high * s0 then sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2 endIf
    n = n + 1
    prev = spot()

2028-01-04
    if prev >= low * s0 and prev <= high * s0 then sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2 endIf
    n = n + 1
    pays variance_notional * (252 * sumsq / n - vol_strike ^ 2)

title: Digital call (cash-or-nothing)
sources: Reiner & Rubinstein, Unscrambling the Binary Code, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Pays a fixed amount if the stock ends above the strike, nothing otherwise.

params.name: payout
params.label: Cash paid if above the strike

script:
# The payout's probability over the model's last step into the expiry,
# given the path before it (lastStepDigital): the same price as the
# threshold, a smaller error, and smooth greeks with no fuzzy smoothing
# (Giles & Szpruch 2012, section 3.5). Under a model with no closed form over its
# last step (rough Bergomi) it is the threshold itself.
#
# Its greeks under Heston, SLV and rough Bergomi come from a second run on
# the threshold smoothed over the strike +- eps (greeks: last-step, #372):
# there the last step's volatility comes near zero (Feller broken) or the
# slot is the threshold, and lastStepDigital's own greeks fail.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    payout = 100
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays payout * lastStepDigital(strike * s0)

title: Digital put (cash-or-nothing)
sources: Reiner & Rubinstein, Unscrambling the Binary Code, Risk, 1991
Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 26 (binary options)
summary: Pays a fixed amount if the stock ends below the strike, nothing otherwise.

params.name: payout
params.label: Cash paid if below the strike

script:
# The mirror of the digital call: together they pay the payout for sure.
# Written on the call's lastStepDigital, the probability over the model's
# last step (Giles & Szpruch 2012, section 3.5): the threshold's price, smooth.
# Its greeks under Heston, SLV and rough Bergomi: as the call's (#372).

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    payout = 100
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays payout * (1 - lastStepDigital(strike * s0))

title: Discount certificate
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: The stock bought at a discount, with the upside capped: long the stock, short a call.

params.name: notional
params.label: Notional of stock at the initial level

script:
# The discount is the price of the call sold, visible in the present value.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    cap = 1.05
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays notional * min(spot() / s0, cap)

title: Dispersion swap
sources: Bossu, Strasser & Guichard, Just What You Need to Know About Variance Swaps, JPMorgan Equity Derivatives, 2005
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Receives the average realised variance of three stocks and pays that of their equally weighted basket: a short position on their correlation.
script:
# Realised variance = 252 / n x sum of squared daily log returns (zero mean),
# for each stock and for the basket of their performances, weights 1/3.

2027-01-04
    variance_notional = 10000
    spread_strike = 0.02
    b0 = spot(0)
    b1 = spot(1)
    b2 = spot(2)
    p0 = spot(0)
    p1 = spot(1)
    p2 = spot(2)
    pb = 1
    q0 = 0
    q1 = 0
    q2 = 0
    qb = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    basket = (spot(0) / b0 + spot(1) / b1 + spot(2) / b2) / 3
    q0 = q0 + log(spot(0) / p0) ^ 2
    q1 = q1 + log(spot(1) / p1) ^ 2
    q2 = q2 + log(spot(2) / p2) ^ 2
    qb = qb + log(basket / pb) ^ 2
    p0 = spot(0)
    p1 = spot(1)
    p2 = spot(2)
    pb = basket
    n = n + 1

2028-01-04
    basket = (spot(0) / b0 + spot(1) / b1 + spot(2) / b2) / 3
    q0 = q0 + log(spot(0) / p0) ^ 2
    q1 = q1 + log(spot(1) / p1) ^ 2
    q2 = q2 + log(spot(2) / p2) ^ 2
    qb = qb + log(basket / pb) ^ 2
    n = n + 1
    pays variance_notional * (252 * ((q0 + q1 + q2) / 3 - qb) / n - spread_strike)

title: Double knock-out call
sources: Kunitomo & Ikeda, Pricing Options with Curved Boundaries, Mathematical Finance, 1992
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call that dies if the stock ever closes outside a range: cheaper than a single barrier, short volatility on both sides.

params.name: low
params.label: Lower knock-out barrier, % of the initial level

params.name: high
params.label: Upper knock-out barrier, % of the initial level

script:
# Both barriers checked at every close (a daily grid approximates continuous
# monitoring). No rebate.
#
# Each close is a knock-out the model conditions on (knockOutAbove /
# knockOutBelow, #369): the step into the close is drawn on the safe side
# and the path carries its survival probability -- the same price as an
# "alive" flag, a smaller error, and greeks with no smoothing. Where the
# model cannot condition, or its conditioned greeks fail (Heston and SLV
# below Feller), the thresholds the knock-outs stand for, smoothed at eps
# for the greeks (greeks: knock-out).

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    low = 0.8
    high = 1.3
    s0 = spot()

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    knockOutBelow(low * s0)
    knockOutAbove(high * s0)

2028-01-04
    knockOutBelow(low * s0)
    knockOutAbove(high * s0)
    pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)

title: Double no-touch
sources: Reiner & Rubinstein, Unscrambling the Binary Code, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Pays a fixed amount if the stock stays strictly inside a range at every close: a bet on low volatility.

params.name: low
params.label: Lower barrier, % of the initial level

params.name: high
params.label: Upper barrier, % of the initial level

script:
# Daily closes, six months.
#
# Each close is a knock-out the model conditions on (knockOutAbove /
# knockOutBelow, #369): the step into the close is drawn on the safe side
# and the path carries its survival probability -- the same price as an
# "alive" flag, a smaller error, and greeks with no smoothing. Where the
# model cannot condition, or its conditioned greeks fail (Heston and SLV
# below Feller), the thresholds the knock-outs stand for, smoothed at eps
# for the greeks (greeks: knock-out).

2027-01-04
    low = 0.85
    high = 1.15
    payout = 100
    s0 = spot()

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-06-30, 1D, US, F)
    knockOutBelow(low * s0)
    knockOutAbove(high * s0)

2027-07-06
    knockOutBelow(low * s0)
    knockOutAbove(high * s0)
    pays payout

title: Down-and-in put
sources: Rubinstein & Reiner, Breaking Down the Barriers, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A put that only comes to life if the stock closes at or below the barrier at some point.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Knock-in barrier, % of the initial level

script:
# Daily closes. The building block of every barrier reverse convertible.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    barrier = 0.7
    s0 = spot()
    ki = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then ki = 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then ki = 1 endIf
    if ki = 1 then pays max(strike * s0 - spot(), 0) endIf

title: Equity forward
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 5 (forward and futures prices)
summary: The obligation to buy the stock at the strike one year later: worth the forward minus the strike, discounted -- linear in the stock, so no volatility enters its price.

params.name: strike
params.label: Delivery price, % of the initial level

script:
# The holder pays the strike and receives the stock at expiry. A futures
# contract settled daily has the same price under a deterministic rate.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    notional = 1
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays notional * (spot() - strike * s0)

title: European call
sources: Black & Scholes, The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities, Journal of Political Economy, 1973
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: The right to buy the stock at its strike level one year later: pays the rise of the stock over the strike, nothing if it ends below.
script:
# Paid in the stock's currency, per share.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)

title: European put
sources: Black & Scholes, The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities, Journal of Political Economy, 1973
Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 15 (the Black-Scholes-Merton model)
summary: The right to sell the stock at its strike level one year later: pays the fall of the stock below the strike, nothing if it ends above.
script:
# Paid in the stock's currency, per share.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays max(strike * s0 - spot(), 0)

title: European swaption
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 29 (swaptions)
Brigo & Mercurio, Interest Rate Models - Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., Springer, 2006, ch. 3.3 (Hull-White: Jamshidian's swaption formula)
summary: The right, in one year, to enter a five-year SOFR swap at the strike: worth the swap at expiry when that is positive, under Hull-White calibrated to the swaptions traded on the market.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike (fixed rate of the swap entered)

params.name: side
params.label: 1 payer (the right to pay the strike), -1 receiver

script:
# At expiry the swap starting then is worth, per unit of notional,
# 1 - P(T0, Tn) - strike * annuity (one curve: SOFR discounts and projects),
# its annuity the sum of yf * df over the annual fixed dates. The holder
# enters it if it is worth more than nothing. df() on the expiry date reads
# the bond prices the simulated short rate gives that day: Hull-White on the
# USD SOFR curve, (a, sigma) calibrated to the at-the-money swaption vols
# implied from the trades DTCC published.

2027-01-04
    strike = 0.046
    notional = 10000000
    side = 1

2028-01-04
    annuity = yf(2028-01-04, 2029-01-04) * df(2029-01-04) + yf(2029-01-04, 2030-01-04) * df(2030-01-04) + yf(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) * df(2031-01-06) + yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05) + yf(2032-01-05, 2033-01-04) * df(2033-01-04)
    swap = 1 - df(2033-01-04) - strike * annuity
    pays notional * max(side * swap, 0)

title: Everest
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A long capital-protected note paying a yearly coupon and, at maturity, the rise of the worst of three stocks.
script:
# Three years. Coupons are guaranteed; the capital is protected, and the
# worst performance is paid if positive.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.02
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)

2028-01-04  2029-01-04
    pays notional * coupon

2030-01-04
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    pays notional * (1 + coupon + max(worst - 1, 0))

title: Fixed-strike lookback call
sources: Goldman, Sosin & Gatto, Path Dependent Options: Buy at the Low, Sell at the High, Journal of Finance, 1979
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on the highest weekly close of the year rather than the final one.
script:
2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()
    hi = spot()

schedule(2027-01-11, 2027-12-27, 1W, US, F)
    hi = max(hi, spot())

2028-01-04
    hi = max(hi, spot())
    pays max(hi - strike * s0, 0)

title: Fixed-rate bond
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 4 (bond pricing)
Fabozzi, Bond Markets, Analysis, and Strategies, 9th ed., Pearson, 2015
summary: Pays a fixed coupon every six months and its face value at maturity: a sum of zero-coupon bonds, one per payment.

params.name: coupon
params.label: Annual coupon rate, % of the face value

script:
# Semiannual coupons of coupon / 2 of the face value, the last with the face
# value. Priced on the government curve of the chosen currency.

2027-01-04
    coupon = 0.04
    notional = 100

schedule(2027-07-05, 2031-07-04, 6M, US, MF)
    pays notional * coupon / 2

2032-01-05
    pays notional * (1 + coupon / 2)

title: Floating-strike lookback call
sources: Goldman, Sosin & Gatto, Path Dependent Options: Buy at the Low, Sell at the High, Journal of Finance, 1979
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Buy at the lowest close of the year: pays the final price minus the minimum close.
script:
# The minimum is taken over every daily close from the strike date on.

2027-01-04
    lo = spot()

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    lo = min(lo, spot())

2028-01-04
    lo = min(lo, spot())
    pays spot() - lo

title: Forward-start call
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call whose strike is set three months from now, at a percentage of the spot on that date: the price of future volatility, not of today's moneyness.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike, % of the spot on the strike date

script:
# The trade starts on 2027-01-04; the strike is fixed three months later, on
# 2027-04-05, and the option matures on 2028-01-04. The first date reads no
# spot: the Price page moves it to the valuation date (start_on), so the
# strike fixing stays three months ahead. Its value depends on the forward
# smile.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0

2027-04-05
    k = strike * spot()

2028-01-04
    pays max(spot() - k, 0)

title: Globally floored cliquet
sources: Wilmott, Cliquet Options and Volatility Models, Wilmott Magazine, 2002
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Twelve monthly returns, each clipped to a range, summed, with a guaranteed minimum on the total.
script:
# The global floor is what makes it sensitive to the forward smile.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    local_floor = -0.03
    local_cap = 0.03
    global_floor = 0.02
    ref = spot()
    total = 0

schedule(2027-02-04, 2027-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    total = total + min(max(spot() / ref - 1, local_floor), local_cap)
    ref = spot()

2028-01-04
    total = total + min(max(spot() / ref - 1, local_floor), local_cap)
    pays notional * max(total, global_floor)

title: Himalaya
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Each year the best performer of the remaining stocks is locked in and removed; pays the average of the locked performances above the strike.

params.name: strike
params.label: Strike on the average locked performance

script:
# Three stocks, three yearly observations. A removed stock gets a
# performance of -1000 so it can never be the best again.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)
    in0 = 1
    in1 = 1
    in2 = 1
    total = 0

2028-01-04  2029-01-04  2030-01-04
    q0 = in0 * spot(0) / s0 - (1 - in0) * 1000
    q1 = in1 * spot(1) / s1 - (1 - in1) * 1000
    q2 = in2 * spot(2) / s2 - (1 - in2) * 1000
    best = max(q0, max(q1, q2))
    total = total + best
    if q0 = best then
        in0 = 0
    else
        if q1 = best then in1 = 0 else in2 = 0 endIf
    endIf

2030-01-07
    pays notional * max(total / 3 - strike, 0)

title: Interest rate swap
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 7 (swaps)
Brigo & Mercurio, Interest Rate Models - Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., Springer, 2006, ch. 1 (interest-rate swaps)
summary: Exchanges a fixed rate for compounded SOFR once a year for five years: worth the floating leg minus the fixed one, both on the SOFR curve built from the swaps traded that day.

params.name: side
params.label: 1 pays the fixed rate (payer), -1 receives it

script:
# Each year the floating leg pays SOFR compounded over the period, worth
# 1 / P(start, end) - 1 at its start: fwdRate(start, end) * yf(start, end),
# paid at the end, hence the df(end). A payer swap pays the fixed rate and
# receives the floating one. Priced on the USD SOFR curve bootstrapped from
# the swaps DTCC published (one curve discounts and projects: SOFR is the
# overnight rate), the short rate's Hull-White calibrated to the swaptions
# traded with them; a swap does not depend on the rate's volatility.

2027-01-04
    fixed_rate = 0.046
    notional = 10000000
    side = 1
    pays side * notional * (fwdRate(2027-01-04, 2028-01-04) - fixed_rate) * yf(2027-01-04, 2028-01-04) * df(2028-01-04)

2028-01-04
    pays side * notional * (fwdRate(2028-01-04, 2029-01-04) - fixed_rate) * yf(2028-01-04, 2029-01-04) * df(2029-01-04)

2029-01-04
    pays side * notional * (fwdRate(2029-01-04, 2030-01-04) - fixed_rate) * yf(2029-01-04, 2030-01-04) * df(2030-01-04)

2030-01-04
    pays side * notional * (fwdRate(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) - fixed_rate) * yf(2030-01-04, 2031-01-06) * df(2031-01-06)

2031-01-06
    pays side * notional * (fwdRate(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) - fixed_rate) * yf(2031-01-06, 2032-01-05) * df(2032-01-05)

title: Ladder call
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: An at-the-money call that locks in gains: once the stock closes above a rung, at least that rung is paid.

params.name: step
params.label: Gap between rungs, % of the initial level

script:
# Three rungs above the initial level, daily closes. Pays the larger of the
# final call and the highest rung reached.

2027-01-04
    step = 0.1
    s0 = spot()
    rung = 1

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() >= (1 + step) * s0 then rung = max(rung, 1 + step) endIf
    if spot() >= (1 + 2 * step) * s0 then rung = max(rung, 1 + 2 * step) endIf
    if spot() >= (1 + 3 * step) * s0 then rung = max(rung, 1 + 3 * step) endIf

2028-01-04
    pays max(max(spot() - s0, 0), (rung - 1) * s0)

title: Napoleon
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Each year pays a fixed coupon plus the worst monthly return of that year, floored at zero; capital back after two years.

params.name: coupon
params.label: Fixed part of the yearly coupon

script:
# Each year's coupon is paid on its anniversary; the capital is repaid with
# the last one.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.08
    ref = spot()
    worst = 1

schedule(2027-02-04, 2027-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    worst = min(worst, spot() / ref - 1)
    ref = spot()

2028-01-04
    worst = min(worst, spot() / ref - 1)
    ref = spot()
    pays notional * max(coupon + worst, 0)
    worst = 1

schedule(2028-02-04, 2028-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    worst = min(worst, spot() / ref - 1)
    ref = spot()

2029-01-04
    worst = min(worst, spot() / ref - 1)
    pays notional * (1 + max(coupon + worst, 0))

title: One-touch (down)
sources: Reiner & Rubinstein, Unscrambling the Binary Code, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Pays a fixed amount at maturity if the stock closes at or below the touch level at least once.

params.name: level
params.label: Touch level, % of the initial level

script:
# Daily closes; paid at maturity, not when touched.

2027-01-04
    level = 0.8
    payout = 100
    s0 = spot()
    touched = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() <= level * s0 then touched = 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot() <= level * s0 then touched = 1 endIf
    if touched = 1 then pays payout endIf

title: Outperformance option
sources: Margrabe, The Value of an Option to Exchange One Asset for Another, Journal of Finance, 1978
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Pays how much the first stock outperformed the second over the year, if it did.
script:
# spot(0) is the stock expected to outperform, spot(1) the benchmark. Its
# value rises as their correlation falls.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    spread = 0.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)

2028-01-04
    pays notional * max(spot(0) / s0 - spot(1) / s1 - spread, 0)

title: Phoenix autocall with memory
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Semi-annual coupons paid when the stock is above the coupon barrier, with missed coupons caught up; redeemed early above the autocall level; capital at risk below the protection barrier at maturity.

params.name: autocall
params.label: Autocall level, % of the initial level

params.name: coupon_barrier
params.label: Coupon barrier, % of the initial level

params.name: protection
params.label: Protection barrier at maturity, % of the initial level

script:
# Below the protection barrier at maturity the capital is repaid in
# proportion to the fall (European knock-in).

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.05
    autocall = 1.0
    coupon_barrier = 0.7
    protection = 0.6
    s0 = spot()
    miss = 0
    alive = 1

2027-07-06  2028-01-04  2028-07-06
    if alive = 1 then
        if spot() >= autocall * s0 then
            pays notional * (1 + coupon * (miss + 1))
            alive = 0
        else
            if spot() >= coupon_barrier * s0 then
                pays notional * coupon * (miss + 1)
                miss = 0
            else
                miss = miss + 1
            endIf
        endIf
    endIf

2029-01-04
    if alive = 1 then
        if spot() >= coupon_barrier * s0 then
            pays notional * (1 + coupon * (miss + 1))
        else
            if spot() < protection * s0 then
                pays notional * spot() / s0
            else
                pays notional
            endIf
        endIf
    endIf

title: Quanto call
sources: Reiner, Quanto Mechanics, Risk 5(3), 1992
Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 30 (quantos)
summary: A call on a stock listed in another currency, its gain paid in dollars at an exchange rate fixed today: the investor takes the stock's risk, not the currency's.

params.name: fixed_rate
params.label: Dollars paid per unit of the stock's currency

script:
# Simulated in dollars: the stock drifts at its own currency's rate, less its
# dividend, less rho sigma_S sigma_X (the quanto adjustment), X its currency
# in dollars.

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    fixed_rate = 1.0
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays fixed_rate * max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)

title: Rainbow call
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on a basket whose weights go by rank: the largest weight on the best performer, the smallest on the worst.
script:
# With three stocks the middle performer is the sum minus the best and the
# worst.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    w_best = 0.5
    w_middle = 0.3
    w_worst = 0.2
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)

2028-01-04
    p0 = spot(0) / s0
    p1 = spot(1) / s1
    p2 = spot(2) / s2
    best = max(p0, max(p1, p2))
    worst = min(p0, min(p1, p2))
    middle = p0 + p1 + p2 - best - worst
    pays notional * max(w_best * best + w_middle * middle + w_worst * worst - 1, 0)

title: Range accrual note
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Earns a coupon on each day the stock closes inside a range around its initial level; capital protected.

params.name: coupon
params.label: Coupon per year if every day is in range

params.name: low
params.label: Lower bound, % of the initial level

params.name: high
params.label: Upper bound, % of the initial level

script:
# Coupon at maturity = coupon x (days in range / days observed).

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.08
    low = 0.9
    high = 1.1
    s0 = spot()
    inside = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    n = n + 1
    if spot() >= low * s0 and spot() <= high * s0 then inside = inside + 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    n = n + 1
    if spot() >= low * s0 and spot() <= high * s0 then inside = inside + 1 endIf
    pays notional * (1 + coupon * inside / n)

title: Reverse cliquet
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A large coupon from which every negative monthly return is subtracted, floored at zero: the investor sells downside volatility.
script:
# Capital protected. Coupon at maturity: max(coupon + sum of the negative
# monthly returns, 0).

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.4
    ref = spot()
    losses = 0

schedule(2027-02-04, 2027-12-04, 1M, US, F)
    losses = losses + min(spot() / ref - 1, 0)
    ref = spot()

2028-01-04
    losses = losses + min(spot() / ref - 1, 0)
    pays notional * (1 + max(coupon + losses, 0))

title: Reverse convertible
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A one-year note paying a high coupon; the capital comes back in full only if the stock ends at or above the strike, otherwise in proportion to its fall.
script:
# The investor is short a put: that premium pays for the coupon.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.1
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot()

2028-01-04
    pays notional * coupon
    if spot() >= strike * s0 then pays notional else pays notional * spot() / (strike * s0) endIf

title: Shark fin note
sources: Rubinstein & Reiner, Breaking Down the Barriers, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A capital-protected note paying the stock's rise, unless the stock ever closes at or above the barrier: then only a rebate on top of the capital.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Knock-out barrier, % of the initial level

params.name: rebate
params.label: Rebate if knocked out, % of notional

script:
# Capital protected at maturity; daily closes. Its payoff chart looks like a
# shark's fin: rising, then a cliff.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    participation = 1.0
    barrier = 1.25
    rebate = 0.05
    s0 = spot()
    alive = 1

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() >= barrier * s0 then alive = 0 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot() >= barrier * s0 then alive = 0 endIf
    if alive = 1 then
        pays notional * (1 + participation * max(spot() / s0 - 1, 0))
    else
        pays notional * (1 + rebate)
    endIf

# The Price page prices it as signed parts (#369 L2b): the paths a knock-out's
# conditioned step simulates never touch the barrier, so the rebate, paid
# where it is touched, is a sure payment less its knock-out --
# E[1{hit} R] = R - E[1{alive} R] -- each part its own run, under the same
# model. The sure part has no variance: what is left is the knock-out's,
# smaller than the hard script's (1.8 times under SLV, the same paths). The
# script above is the product as one hard script.

title: Twin-win certificate
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Gains whichever way the stock moves, as long as it never closes at or below the barrier.
script:
# Above the barrier the investor earns the absolute performance; once
# touched, plain stock.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    barrier = 0.7
    s0 = spot()
    hit = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then hit = 1 endIf

2028-01-04
    if spot() <= barrier * s0 then hit = 1 endIf
    if hit = 0 then
        pays notional * (1 + abs(spot() / s0 - 1))
    else
        pays notional * spot() / s0
    endIf

title: Up-and-out call
sources: Rubinstein & Reiner, Breaking Down the Barriers, Risk, 1991
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call that dies if the stock ever closes at or above the barrier.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Knock-out barrier, % of the initial level

script:
# Barrier checked at every close (a daily grid approximates continuous
# monitoring). No rebate.
#
# Each close is a knock-out the model conditions on (knockOutAbove /
# knockOutBelow, #369): the step into the close is drawn on the safe side
# and the path carries its survival probability -- the same price as an
# "alive" flag, a smaller error, and greeks with no smoothing. Where the
# model cannot condition, or its conditioned greeks fail (Heston and SLV
# below Feller), the thresholds the knock-outs stand for, smoothed at eps
# for the greeks (greeks: knock-out).

2027-01-04
    strike = 1.0
    barrier = 1.3
    s0 = spot()

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    knockOutAbove(barrier * s0)

2028-01-04
    knockOutAbove(barrier * s0)
    pays max(spot() - strike * s0, 0)

title: Variance swap
sources: Demeterfi, Derman, Kamal & Zou, A Guide to Volatility and Variance Swaps, Journal of Derivatives, 1999
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Exchanges the realised variance of daily returns over a year for a fixed volatility strike squared.
script:
# Realised variance = 252 / n x sum of squared daily log returns (zero mean).

2027-01-04
    variance_notional = 10000
    vol_strike = 0.2
    prev = spot()
    sumsq = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2
    n = n + 1
    prev = spot()

2028-01-04
    sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2
    n = n + 1
    pays variance_notional * (252 * sumsq / n - vol_strike ^ 2)

title: Volatility swap
sources: Demeterfi, Derman, Kamal & Zou, A Guide to Volatility and Variance Swaps, Journal of Derivatives, 1999
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Exchanges realised volatility (not variance) for a fixed strike.
script:
# Realised volatility = sqrt(252 / n x sum of squared daily log returns).

2027-01-04
    vega_notional = 1000
    vol_strike = 0.2
    prev = spot()
    sumsq = 0
    n = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2
    n = n + 1
    prev = spot()

2028-01-04
    sumsq = sumsq + log(spot() / prev) ^ 2
    n = n + 1
    pays 100 * vega_notional * (sqrt(252 * sumsq / n) - vol_strike)

title: Worst-of Phoenix autocall
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: The most traded structured product: quarterly coupons while the worst of three stocks is above the coupon barrier, early redemption above the autocall level, capital at risk below the protection barrier at maturity.
script:
# Two years, quarterly observations on the worst performer, no coupon
# memory.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.025
    autocall = 1.0
    coupon_barrier = 0.7
    protection = 0.6
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)
    alive = 1

schedule(2027-04-05, 2028-10-04, 3M, US, F)
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    if alive = 1 then
        if worst >= autocall then
            pays notional * (1 + coupon)
            alive = 0
        else
            if worst >= coupon_barrier then pays notional * coupon endIf
        endIf
    endIf

2029-01-04
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    if alive = 1 then
        if worst >= coupon_barrier then
            pays notional * (1 + coupon)
        else
            if worst < protection then pays notional * worst else pays notional endIf
        endIf
    endIf

title: Worst-of call
sources: Stulz, Options on the Minimum or the Maximum of Two Risky Assets, Journal of Financial Economics, 1982
Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: A call on the worst performer of three stocks: it pays only if all three rose, so it is cheap and long correlation.
script:
2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    strike = 1.0
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)

2028-01-04
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    pays notional * max(worst - strike, 0)

title: Worst-of barrier reverse convertible
sources: Bouzoubaa & Osseiran, Exotic Options and Hybrids: A Guide to Structuring, Pricing and Trading, Wiley, 2010
summary: Quarterly coupons on three stocks; the capital is at risk if the worst of them ever closes at or below the barrier and ends below its initial level.

params.name: barrier
params.label: Knock-in barrier on the worst, % of initial

script:
# Knock-in on the worst performer, daily closes. The higher coupon than a
# single-stock version pays for the short correlation.

2027-01-04
    notional = 1000
    coupon = 0.03
    barrier = 0.6
    s0 = spot(0)
    s1 = spot(1)
    s2 = spot(2)
    ki = 0

schedule(2027-01-05, 2027-12-30, 1D, US, F)
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    if worst <= barrier then ki = 1 endIf

2027-04-05  2027-07-06  2027-10-04
    pays notional * coupon

2028-01-04
    worst = min(spot(0) / s0, min(spot(1) / s1, spot(2) / s2))
    if worst <= barrier then ki = 1 endIf
    pays notional * coupon
    if ki = 1 and worst < 1 then pays notional * worst else pays notional endIf

title: Zero-coupon bond
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed., Pearson, ch. 4 (zero rates and bond pricing)
Brigo & Mercurio, Interest Rate Models - Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., Springer, 2006, ch. 1
summary: Pays its face value once, at maturity, and nothing before: its price is the discount factor to that date.
script:
# Priced on the government curve of the chosen currency, by Hull-White fitted
# to it (Monte-Carlo) or by the curve itself (Analytic): the same price, the
# short rate's volatility only adds noise to a payment that does not depend
# on it.

2027-01-04
    notional = 100

2032-01-05
    pays notional
